findings.title: Groups VIEW scope is treated as manage
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() passes both VIEW and MANAGE to hasPermission and returns true if either scope is granted. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup authorizes only with requireManage(), so an admin who was granted view-only on groups can create top-level groups and can move an existing group to the top of the tree by posting its id. canManage(GroupModel) correctly requires MANAGE, and UserPermissions.canManage() does not treat view as manage. The new GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage() javadoc repeats this incorrect contract and should be corrected with the implementation.

findings.title: Member-view filter stores authorization resource ids, not group ids
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is the set UsersResource.getUsersCount, UsersResource.searchForUser, and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser apply as the groups whose members the caller may see. The findByType callback passes groupResource.getId() (the authorization resource primary key) both into hasPermission() and into the returned set. hasPermission() looks up resources by name, and per-group resources are named with the group id, so the lookup misses the group, falls back to the all-groups resource, and ignores the per-group view-members/manage-members grant. The ids placed in the session UserModel.GROUPS attribute are not group ids, and the schema resource named "Groups" is itself included by findByType. User search then matches nobody, so paginated results omit users the admin is allowed to see; when the set is empty, the query is not constrained and getUsersCount returns 0 while the list path only filters later in memory. GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest only calls users().search and never checks counts, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Per-group authz resources are created without a type
findings.body: getOrCreateResource() creates the per-object resource and updates scopes, but never calls setType(resourceType). V1 GroupPermissions.initialize did set the type. GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() discovers groups with resourceStore.findByType(server, "Groups"), so individual group resources are invisible to that scan and view-members/manage-members grants never contribute real group ids to the user-search filter. Only the schema-level resource created in init(), which does set type, is found. Because the type is also unset, an evaluator that applies resource-type policies only to typed resources will not apply all-groups policies to these rows either.

findings.title: Group deletion hits unsupported V2 setPermissionsEnabled
findings.body: AdminPermissions.registerListener still handles every GroupRemovedEvent by calling management().groups().setPermissionsEnabled(group, false) when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 also enabled, groups() is now GroupPermissionsV2, and setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException. The listener is invoked from realm.removeGroup with no catch, so deleting any group (not only groups that have permissions) fails with a 500 and rolls back. V1 fine-grained admin authz is commonly enabled together with V2. If only V2 is enabled, the listener is not registered at all because it checks the V1 feature, so authorization resources created for a group by getOrCreateResource are never removed when the group is deleted. The same throw breaks the V1 management/permissions admin endpoint, which calls setPermissionsEnabled after requiring ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ.

findings.title: All-groups policies are skipped once a per-group resource exists
findings.body: hasPermission() evaluates only the per-group resource when findByName finds one, and loads the Groups type resource only when that lookup returns null. getOrCreateResource creates that row as soon as any permission references the group, including a different admin or a different scope such as view-members. After that, GroupPermissionsV2 never consults all-groups allow or deny policies for that group: an admin with all-groups MANAGE loses update, delete, and membership checks on it, and a negative all-groups policy does not deny a scope granted by the specific resource. Group listing no longer short-circuits on canView(), so those groups also disappear from an admin who only has all-groups view. testManageAllGroups only updates a group that has no specific resource, so only the fallback path is tested.

findings.title: Existing admin-permissions clients never receive the Groups schema
findings.body: init() returns immediately when the realm already has an admin-permissions client, so upgrade does not add the Groups resource type, the "Groups" all-resource, or the new scopes manage-membership, manage-members, and view-members. On those realms, creating a group permission fails: getScope throws ModelValidationException because the scope does not exist, and getOrCreateResource throws ModelException ("No scopes found") when attaching scopes. GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission then gets a null type resource from getResourceTypeResource and passes it to policyStore.findByResource and resource.getScopes(), which are not null-safe, so group list and permission checks for fine-grained admins throw NullPointerException instead of denying. This pull request contains no migration.

findings.title: Scope grants are accepted without matching the evaluated resource
findings.body: After evaluatePermission, GroupPermissionsV2 returns true for any permission whose scopes intersect the requested scopes. UserPermissionsV2, which this evaluator copies, ignores permissions whose resource id is not the resource just evaluated, because the result is not guaranteed to contain only that resource. Omitting the check here can apply a scope granted on another resource to the group being checked, widening view, manage, view-members, manage-members, or manage-membership beyond that group's policies.

findings.title: Group list runs a policy evaluation per group
findings.body: V2 canView(GroupModel) does not reuse the no-arg canView() result, and GroupsResource.getGroups and GroupResource.getSubGroups dropped the previous canViewGlobal short-circuit. An admin whose access comes from an all-groups permission therefore runs a full authorization evaluation for every group on the page, even though each call falls back to the same Groups type resource. On realms with large group trees the groups admin API issues one policy evaluation, and several store queries, per group on every list request.

findings.title: Group permission resources have no resolvable name
findings.body: getResourceName() maps Users resources to the username, but a Groups resource falls through to resource.getDisplayName(). getOrCreateResource() stores the group id as the resource name and never sets a display name, so the authorization admin API shows a null name, or a raw id, for group permissions instead of the group name. After the group is deleted or renamed those resources stay unresolved, whereas a missing user at least throws ModelIllegalStateException.

findings.title: requireManageMembers javadoc cites the wrong method
findings.body: The javadoc on requireManageMembers says it throws ForbiddenException if canManageMembership(GroupModel) returns false. The implementation throws when canManageMembers returns false. Those are different scopes (manage-membership versus manage-members), so the published contract on this permission interface is wrong.
